messages:
Marco: Heads-up — I'm building a per-route cost widget that shows token cost, cache credits, and fallback-model delta.
Priya: Nice. Are we attributing cache savings to the request route or the tenant? edge case: shared prefix cache across tenants.
Marco: Proposal: two columns — "charged_tokens" and "cache_saved_tokens (credited)". Credit policy: if prefix served by tenant-specific KV then credit tenant; if served by global cache, do proportional split by recent traffic weight.
Jen: Proportional split is noisy. Can we tag cache entries with "last_writer" metadata? we already write origin sometimes.
Alex: We don't persist origin reliably (evictions/compaction). Adding last_writer increases write amplification. Alternative: sampling-based attribution in telemetry.
Priya: Sampling sounds reasonable but we need SLA for accuracy. For billing we need deterministic-ish numbers.
ops-bot: :loudspeaker: deploy: cost-dashboard-sample -> staging (sha: b7f3c1d)
Marco: For per-model/unit economics we also need model_variant (e.g., fp16, int8) since per-token cost differs a lot.
Jen: UX: when a route falls back to a cheaper model under load, the dashboard should show both actual cost and a "no-fallback" hypothetical to surface savings vs quality delta.
Alex: We can compute "no-fallback" offline by replaying routing traces with fallback disabled. heavy but ok as a nightly job.
Priya: Quotas issue: tenants see quota hits because fallback generates extra tokens on downstream models — we need transparent attribution to avoid double-charging.
Marco: Agreed. Plan: add a "token attribution ledger" per billing window with categories: billed_tokens, credited_cache_tokens, overhead_tokens (fallback delta).
Jen: Telemetry schema suggestion: include fields: route_id, tenant_id, model_variant, fallback_reason, latency_ms, request_tokens, response_tokens.
Marco: Also include batching metadata: batch_size, batching_window_ms so we can estimate per-token latency/cost.
Alex: SQL snippet for rollups: 
``` 
SELECT route_id,
       SUM(response_tokens) AS total_tokens,
       SUM(CASE WHEN cache_hit THEN response_tokens ELSE 0 END) AS cached_tokens,
       SUM(CASE WHEN fallback_used THEN response_tokens ELSE 0 END) AS fallback_tokens
FROM events.inference
WHERE ts >= '2026-03-01'
GROUP BY route_id;
```
Priya: For cache attribution sampling: emit cache.inspect events on 0.1% of requests with full trace + cache_entry_owner. Use that to calibrate proportional splits.
Jen: On the console, propose: sparkline for cost trend, top-10 routes table (cost, cache credits, avg latency), and a "replay hypothetical" button that queues the nightly job.
Marco: Backend endpoint: I'll add `/internal/cost/rollup?start=&end=&granularity=` to return per-route rollups. It will accept preview=true to run sample replay.
Alex: I'll add instrumentation in inference service to emit events: `inference.request`, `inference.response`, `cache.hit`, `cache.eviction`, each including model_variant and token_counts.
Priya: Also add `routing.decision` with fields: route_id, selected_model, fallback_flag, reason.
ops-bot: :link: Design doc PR: https://github.com/redwoodinc/cost-dashboard/pull/412 (needs UX mocks)
Marco: I'll open a follow-up thread with UI mocks and a small data contract.
Jen: tl;dr: telemetry event + ledger model + sampling plan for cache attribution + nightly replay for hypothetical costs + console widgets + CSV export for billing.
Priya: +1 for CSV export and explicit notes for quota reconciliation.
Marco: Thanks — I'll draft the data contract and a short RFC today and tag infra and billing teams.
